## QUESTION

1. __Take time to get to know your data.__ Based on some initial exploration, identify 3 variables in the dataset you think will have strong predictive ability for determining if a house was built before 1980. Explain/justify the reasoning behind your guesses (for example with plots).

Quality of the home is a great variable since after 1987 the number of homes ranked quality "C" gets proportionally lower and the proportion of quality "A" and "B" homes goes up significantly. Likewise there is a good fingerprint based on architectural styles throughout the decades with a clear shift towards two story homes in the years after 1980. At first I treated those two as one variable each but Ryan said they count as multiple for each.

```{python}
# Optional: code you used to get to know your data
df_year_quality = df.group_by("yrbuilt").agg(quality_a_homes = pl.col("quality_A").sum(),
quality_b_homes = pl.col("quality_B").sum(),
quality_c_homes = pl.col("quality_C").sum(),
quality_d_homes = pl.col("quality_D").sum(),
quality_x_homes = pl.col("quality_X").sum()).sort("yrbuilt", descending=True)

quality_columns = [c for c in df_year_quality.columns if c.startswith("quality_")]



df_quality_proportions = df_year_quality.with_columns(total_homes = pl.sum_horizontal(pl.all().exclude("yrbuilt"))).with_columns((pl.col(quality_columns) / pl.col("total_homes")).name.suffix("_proportion")).filter(pl.col("total_homes") >=10)

quality_proportions_columns = [c for c in df_quality_proportions.columns if c.endswith("_proportion")]

df_long_quality_proportions = df_quality_proportions.unpivot(index="yrbuilt", on=quality_proportions_columns, variable_name="quality", value_name="proportion")

```

1. __Build a classification model labeling houses as being built “before 1980” or “during or after 1980”.__ Your goal is to reach or exceed 90% accuracy. Report your final model choice and any other model parameters you may have tweaked (train-test split ratio, tuning parameters, etc).  

I was surpised to see that Garage type was the highest weighted attribute. I was also surprised to see it's percentage being only 3.35% and the total of all the weights adding up to just 25.90%. I had assumed that the weights should always add up to 1.0, but I surmise the meaning of this finding is that no one attribute was incredibly accurate at predicting if a house was built before 1980 or not. I used the RandomForestClassifier model and used the default parameters with a test_size of 0.2 and a random_state of 28. This got me to 93% accuracy so I did not experiment further. For my attributes I selected all numeric columns other than "yrbuilt" and "before1980" and my target was "before1980".

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
# Don't forget, you need another import statement to import the desired ML model from sklearn
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, confusion_matrix, ConfusionMatrixDisplay
from sklearn.inspection import permutation_importance
import polars.selectors as cs

x = df.select(cs.numeric().exclude(["before1980","yrbuilt"]))
y = df.select("before1980")

x_train, x_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(x, y, test_size=0.2, random_state=28)

rf_classifier = RandomForestClassifier()
rf_classifier.fit(x_train, y_train)

rf_pred = rf_classifier.predict(x_test)

print(classification_report(y_test, rf_pred))

rf_cm=confusion_matrix(y_test, rf_pred)
rf_disp = ConfusionMatrixDisplay(confusion_matrix = rf_cm)

ConfusionMatrixDisplay.from_estimator(rf_classifier, x_test, y_test, cmap="Greens")

rf_result= permutation_importance(rf_classifier, x_test, y_test, n_repeats=4,random_state=28)

rf_perms_imp = pl.DataFrame({'importance':rf_result.importances_mean, 'vars':x_train.columns})

with pl.Config(tbl_rows=-1, tbl_cols=-1, fmt_str_lengths=1000):
    display(
      print(rf_perms_imp.sort(['importance'], descending=True))
    )

importance_sum = rf_perms_imp.with_columns(sum = pl.col("importance").sum())
```
